title: Sar Pass Trek
reportingPoint: Kasol. The exact meeting point and reporting time are shared once your booking is confirmed.
highlights: Camping at Mung Thach, Nagaru and Biskeri Thach
Trail through rhododendron and pine forest, meadows and snow
Views of the Chandrakhani range from Mung Thach and of Manikaran from Nagaru
All meals, permits, trekking equipment and a certified trek leader
overview:
Sar Pass is a 13,800 ft pass above Kasol, a village in the Kullu region of Himachal Pradesh, and the trek to it is usually done in the summer months (April to June), when there is snow on the route. This **4 Nights / 5 Days** trek runs Kasol to Kasol: you need to reach Kasol on your own, and the meeting point and reporting time are shared once your booking is confirmed.

Day 1 is the trek from Kasol to Grahan village, with a night in a local guesthouse. Day 2 climbs through forest to the camp at Mung Thach, and Day 3 continues up a steep ridge to the Nagaru campsite. Day 4 is the early climb in snow to Sar Pass, followed by the descent to the camp at Biskeri Thach. Day 5 comes down through Pulga, Tulga and Barshaini and returns to Kasol. Camping, all meals, permits, trekking equipment and a trek leader are included. Departures are every Saturday and Sunday. Prices start at ₹6,499 per person on triple sharing (5% GST extra); dual sharing is ₹7,499 per person.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kasol to Grahan village
itinerary.content:
Start from Kasol and trek along the left bank of the Grahan Nallah.
The first part of the trail is straightforward and is used regularly by locals.
Away from the river, the trail gets rockier and climbs into a rhododendron forest, which blooms in season.
Reach Grahan village, the last settlement with mobile network on the route.
Overnight stay at a local guesthouse in Grahan.

itinerary.title: Trek from Grahan village to Mung Thach
itinerary.content:
Leave Grahan and head north towards Mung Thach on a trail commonly used by villagers.
Get the first views of distant points such as Sar Top and the Nagaru ridge.
The trail gets steeper and more demanding as it climbs through dense forest.
Mung Thach has views of the Chandrakhani range.
Overnight camping in the forest at Mung Thach.

itinerary.title: Trek from Mung Thach to Nagaru
itinerary.content:
Trek from Mung Thach towards Nagaru; the path may be under snow.
The route includes a steep climb up a ridge, which needs care, especially in snow.
Reach the Nagaru campsite, with views of Manikaran and the surrounding mountains.
The camp faces north, so expect a cold night.
Overnight camping at Nagaru.

itinerary.title: Nagaru to Biskeri Thach via Sar Pass
itinerary.content:
Start early for the steep ascent in snow to Sar Pass.
Take in the panoramic views from the pass and stop for photographs.
The descent includes a slide down towards Biskeri, done with proper precautions.
Continue through valleys and across streams to Biskeri Thach.
Overnight camping among the meadows and pine forest at Biskeri Thach.

itinerary.title: Trek from Biskeri Thach to Kasol
itinerary.content:
Trek down from Biskeri Thach through dense forest and cross a brook.
The path splits towards the twin villages of Pulga and Tulga, divided by the creek, and continues to Barshaini.
Cross the Parvati River and return to Kasol, where the trek ends.

faqs.q: Where does the trek start and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The trek starts and ends in Kasol, in the Kullu region of Himachal Pradesh. You travel to and from Kasol yourself. The exact meeting point and reporting time are shared once your booking is confirmed.

faqs.q: How much does the Sar Pass Trek cost?
faqs.a: ₹6,499 per person on triple sharing and ₹7,499 per person on dual sharing. 5% GST is extra.
Departures are every Saturday and Sunday. The trek is usually done in the summer months, from April to June, when there is snow on the route.
Sar Pass is at an elevation of 13,800 ft. It is crossed on Day 4, with an early start from Nagaru and a steep ascent in snow.

Pick-up and drop transfers from Kasol to Kasol, a guesthouse night in Grahan and camping at Mung Thach, Nagaru and Biskeri Thach (dome tents on triple sharing or alpine tents on quad sharing), all 3 meals plus snacks, trekking and forest permits, campsite fees, trekking equipment, a certified trek leader, a trek crew, safety gear and a trek certificate of completion. Porter or mule charges, insurance and food during the transfers are not included.

faqs.q: What do I need to carry?
faqs.a: Non-skid, deep-treaded hiking shoes, lightweight slippers or sandals, track pants, full-sleeve T-shirts, rainwear, a sun cap, sunscreen and lip balm, a toiletries kit, dry fruits and chocolate bars, a power bank and your personal medicines. Carry a valid government-approved photo ID as well. The full list is under Things To Pack.

faqs.q: How do I book and pay?
faqs.a: Reserve your seat by paying 50% of the trip cost, and pay the rest at least 4 days before the trip. 5% GST is added to the price.

Cancel more than 10 days before the travel date and 50% of the advance is refunded; 5 to 10 days before, 25% of the advance; less than 5 days before, there is no refund. There is no refund for no-shows or early check-outs.
